time.desc: The academic resource platform removed the master's degree thesis of the party involved from the public page, raising questions about the triggering mechanism of the removal and the role of the school.
The master's degree thesis of the party involved was downloaded more than 310,000 times before it was removed, ranking first among the school's literature sources.

The platform’s customer service stated that the author must contact the school’s graduate school to issue a retraction letter before withdrawing the dissertation. There was no clear response as to whether the school could issue a letter directly without the author’s application.

The second instance of the civil infringement dispute made a final ruling and upheld the conclusion of the first instance, confirming that the existing evidence was insufficient to support the claim of sexual harassment.

The party involved filed an appeal to the higher court within about 20 days after losing the first instance. During this period, someone called the court and learned that the case was being heard in the second instance.

The accused party filed an appeal last year after losing the first instance of an administrative lawsuit against relevant institutions regarding demerit penalties. As of this stage, the final result has not been made public.
The party committee secretary of the university involved was replaced, and the new secretary took office

The university involved issued a formal notice: revoking the disciplinary sanctions against the accused students and announcing review and accountability, while maintaining the validity of the other party’s degree.
In the review notification, the school suspended the relevant tutors' enrollment qualifications for two years, and gave several managers intra-party warnings or admonishments.
The school clarified in the briefing that the rumor that a relative of the accuser holds a certain title within the school is untrue.
In the report, the university involved focused on refuting a number of key online rumors, further triggering controversy over the credibility of the report and the boundaries of textual expression.
The university involved formed a five-member expert team to complete the review and announced the scale of the investigation and the conclusion that the paper did not involve plagiarism.

The school established a five-member expert team to complete the reexamination, investigated 21 people, reviewed 91 pieces of evidence, and determined that the paper was not plagiarized and the degree was not revoked.
The party involved spoke out intensively on social platforms to confront the outside world and defend themselves, which promoted a new round of negative focus in public opinion on the incident.
The party involved posted and quickly denied claims related to public job examinations on social platforms, which was deemed by public opinion as false information to create a topic.
